test_title: PYST 18: Selection Post (Higher Secondary Level) - GA (Held On 30 Jul, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: How does IMEC alliance benefit Indian exporters?

options.text: Reduced transportation time and lower logistics costs
Increased import duties on European goods
Limited access to Middle Eastern markets

solution:
The correct answer is __**Reduced transportation time and lower logistics costs**__

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC)** is a landmark infrastructure project aimed at boosting **economic growth** and **connectivity** between Asia, the Arabian Gulf, and Europe.

• The primary benefit for **Indian exporters** is the significant reduction in **transit time** and **logistics costs**. It is estimated that the corridor will make trade with Europe **40% faster** compared to the current **Suez Canal** route.

• By integrating **railway lines** and **ship-to-rail** transit networks, the corridor reduces the reliance on long maritime routes, thereby lowering **transportation expenses** by approximately **30%**.

• This efficiency makes **Indian goods** more competitive in international markets, particularly in the **Middle East** and **European Union**.

• The other options are incorrect because **increased duties**, **limited access**, or **higher tariffs** would act as barriers to trade, whereas **IMEC** is designed to facilitate and expand trade.

**Additional Information__**

• The **IMEC** was officially announced on the sidelines of the **G20 Summit** held in **New Delhi** in **September 2023**.

• The project is part of the **Partnership for Global Infrastructure and Investment (PGII)**, a G7 initiative to fund infrastructure projects in developing nations.

• The corridor consists of two separate parts: the **East Corridor** connecting India to the Arabian Gulf and the **Northern Corridor** connecting the Arabian Gulf to Europe.

• Key participating entities include **India**, the **United Arab Emirates (UAE)**, **Saudi Arabia**, the **European Union**, **France**, **Italy**, **Germany**, and the **United States**.

• Beyond transport, the corridor will also include **undersea cables** for data transmission and pipelines for **clean hydrogen** export.
